headline.text: The FDA buprenorphine label says no interactions with buprenorphine are expected for NRTIs as a class.

reported.text: The statement covers NRTIs as a class and does not name abacavir.

mechanism.text: The label says NRTIs do not appear to induce or inhibit the P450 enzyme pathway.

claims.text: The FDA buprenorphine label says nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors do not appear to induce or inhibit the P450 pathway, so no interactions with buprenorphine are expected.
claims.quote: Nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors (NRTIs) do not appear to induce or inhibit the P450 enzyme pathway, thus no interactions with buprenorphine are expected.
claims.judgeRationale: Quote is the buprenorphine label NRTI class statement and abacavir is an NRTI; the claim reproduces it accurately.

sources.title: Ombitasvir/Paritaprevir/Ritonavir and Dasabuvir: Drug Interactions With Antiretroviral Agents and Drugs forSubstance Abuse.
sources.citation: 2160-7648 6 2 2017 Mar Clinical pharmacology in drug development Clin Pharmacol Drug Dev

pharmacistQuestions.text: The label describes this interaction, but there seem to be no human studies of it. How is it usually handled for someone like me?
Do any of my other medicines contain Abacavir or Buprenorphine, or work the same way?
Does my dose, or the time between taking Abacavir and Buprenorphine, change how much this matters?

gaps.text: No controlled human study of this combination was found in the PubMed search.
